sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2022. Reconstructing non-contrastive stress in Austronesian and the role of the mora in stress shift, gemination and vowel shift. Diachronica 40(1): 111-152.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Borneo-wide stress survey; Tunjung is not mentioned (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing); only generic 'Greater Barito' references to Sama-Bajaw.

sources.citation: Bety, Nur. 2021. Deret vokal dan deret konsonan dalam bahasa Tunjung (Tonyooi). LOA: Jurnal Ketatabahasaan dan Kesusastraan 16(2): 142-152. doi:10.26499/loa.v16i2.4131
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonotactics only (vowel/consonant sequences). p.146: in vowel sequences like ja-in 'buruk', ba-okng 'bau', 'baik a maupun i atau a dan u masing-masing mendapat tekanan yang (hampir) sama dan membentuk suku kata tersendiri' (each vowel gets (almost) equal stress and forms its own syllable) -- an argument for heterosyllabicity, not a word-stress rule. No suprasegmental section.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: a comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Primary Tunjung field data (consultant 'Son', Sendawar); sec. 2.7 Barito and 2.7.3.3 Barito-Mahakam (PDF pp.168-176) give segmental historical phonology only. The word 'stress' does not occur in the Barito section; stress is discussed only for Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi and W. Kalimantan Malayic. Silent on Tunjung stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert & Alexander D. Smith. 2014. A bibliography of the languages of Borneo (and Madagascar). Phillips: Borneo Research Council.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography: Tunjung appears only in the language roster, the Hudson 1967 comment ('sole published vocabulary for Tunjung'), the Boutin 2000 comment (nasal preplosion) and Pusat Bahasa Swadesh-list volumes; no grammar or phonology of Tunjung is listed.

sources.citation: Hudson, Alfred B. 1967. The Barito isolects of Borneo: a classification based on comparative reconstruction and lexicostatistics. Data Paper 68. Ithaca: Cornell SEAP. hdl:1813/57536

sources.note: 'Tundjung' (Muara Bunjut) represented by an incomplete Swadesh list only; comparative sound correspondences; eCommons scanned text has 0 hits for stress/accent. Silent.
